title: What a GPU answer may be used for

blocks.text: A port authority plans its capital works with a MILP that **maximises** value, and its nightly service now has GPU answers on hand. Its rule: a GPU answer may serve as an **LP bound** or as a **start** for the CPU solver, each verified on the CPU, and never as the **plan of record**.
Write `usable(use, gpu, cpu)` in `answers.py`, returning `(accepted, value)` where `value` is the thing to use when accepted and a reason when not:

items: `use == "plan"`: never; the reason is `"the plan of record runs on the CPU"`.

`use == "bound"`: `gpu` is `{"status", "objective"}` from an LP relaxation and `cpu` is `{"objective"}` from a CPU solve of the same LP. Refuse with `"not optimal"` unless the GPU status is `"Optimal"`; refuse with `"not confirmed"` unless the two objectives differ by at most $`10^{-6}`$ relatively (divided by $`\max(1, \lvert\text{CPU objective}\rvert)`$). Otherwise use the **larger** of the two values: a bound on a maximisation must not understate the cap.

`use == "start"`: `gpu` is `{"status", "x"}` from a MILP solver and `cpu` is `{"feasible", "integral"}`, the CPU check of `x`. Use `x` when both checks passed, whatever the status label says; otherwise refuse with `"fails the check"`.

blocks.text:
from __future__ import annotations


def usable(use: str, gpu: dict, cpu: dict) -> tuple[bool, object]:
    """May a GPU answer serve this use of a maximisation model? Returns (accepted, value or reason).

    use "bound": gpu {"status", "objective"} from an LP relaxation; cpu {"objective"} from a CPU solve.
    use "start": gpu {"status", "x"} from a MILP; cpu {"feasible", "integral"} from the CPU check of x.
    use "plan": the plan of record.
    """
    match use:
        case "plan":
            return False, "the plan of record runs on the CPU"
        case "bound":
            if gpu["status"] != "Optimal":
                return False, "not optimal"
            if abs(gpu["objective"] - cpu["objective"]) > 1e-6 * max(1.0, abs(cpu["objective"])):
                return False, "not confirmed"
            return True, max(gpu["objective"], cpu["objective"])
        case "start":
            if cpu["feasible"] and cpu["integral"]:
                return True, gpu["x"]
            return False, "fails the check"
    return False, "unknown use"


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(usable("bound", {"status": "Optimal", "objective": 10.0}, {"objective": 10.0}))

cases.says: an LP bound the CPU confirms is used, and one it does not is refused
the plan of record never comes from the GPU
a start that passed the CPU check is used whatever its status label
a bound on a maximisation is reported at the larger of the two values
confirmation is relative to the objective's size
a bound whose solver did not report it optimal is not used

origin.section: A GPU Result Serves a Capital Plan Only as a Bound or a Start, Verified on the CPU

concepts: a GPU answer serves as a confirmed bound or a checked start, never as the plan of record
